text:
maria: Heads up - noticing a p99 jump for short requests after yesterday's kernel-selector change. seq<=32 p99 went from ~22ms to ~68ms on host-side paths. No model change.

aj: ugh. can you paste the flame or a short profile? is it CPU or syscall tail? :eyes:

siddharth: quick perf dump from the canary box (samples):
```
  28% grpc_writev (host-side)
  19% http2_window_update (net)
  15% request_parse_tokenizer
  12% kernel_selector::choose_slow_path_for_short_seq
  10% kv_cache_lookup (miss)
  8% other
```
seems dominated by writev + window pressure + parse cost.

kevin: that `choose_slow_path_for_short_seq` bit looks suspicious. we added a conservative heuristic to avoid vectorized kernels for certain packing shapes. for very short sequences the selector appears to pick a non-packed path that triggers extra header concat and small writes. small writes + HTTP/2 windowing -> writev stalls.

maria: also seeing a correlation with KV cache misses: when metadata shard isn't found we reparse headers and reallocate buffers which amplifies the write bursts. single-request hot path gets 3 extra allocs.

aj: any easy mitigations to roll right now?

kevin: two quick things we can try as a hotfix: 1) force fast-path kernel for seq<=48 on host runtime (override selector) 2) increase writev coalescing threshold to 8KB for the next hour to avoid many tiny frames. both are config flags, can canary.

siddharth: I'll add a microbench for seq=8/16/32 to reproduce selector decision matrix. will include exact input shapes and batch sizes.

ops-bot: deploy triggered by kevin: host-runtime/override-kernel-flag -> canary (3 hosts)

maria: canary looks good so far, p99 back to ~24ms on the 3 hosts. still want the selector fix + KV miss path audit. opening a follow-up issue for KV shard fallback behavior.

aj: nice. please add a small regression test so future selector tweaks don't regress short-seq latency.

kevin: agreed. I'll send a PR that: adds unit tests for selector matrix, instruments KV miss path with a lightweight counter, and makes the writev threshold configurable via env.

maria: thanks — tracking in #perf with link to the canary logs and the flame. will update when PR lands. :thumbsup:
